The feature matrix was built from **4 signals × 7 bacteria × 5 replicates**. Every probe–bacterium reaction was run in quintuplicate, and the data were analysed with LDA (Table S1) (paper2, p. 6). That works out to 140 measurements in total, though the paper does not state this number itself.

The seven bacteria were *P. aeruginosa*, *E. coli*, *E. sakazakii*, *S. typhimurium*, *E. faecium*, *L. monocytogenes* and *S. aureus* (paper2, p. 3).

The paper does not name the four signals at this point. It describes the readouts as CD plus RGB colorimetric signals (paper2, pp. 1, 3), and the Fig. 3 heat maps are labelled "CD/RGB signal" (paper2, p. 6). This suggests the four are CD, R, G and B, but that is my inference rather than an explicit statement.
question: How many signals, bacteria and replicates made up the feature matrix for pattern recognition?
